hypothesis_loop.selection_reason: B10 Norway cabins generated RISK_PRICER_SUBSIDIZES_PREVENTION and ABSENCE_AMPLIFIES_DAMAGE_SEVERITY. B11 tests those mechanisms in a different country and buyer structure: UK rental/commercial property portfolios, where insurers, water regulators/utilities and professional property owners can all capture avoided loss.
hypothesis_loop.hypothesis: Leak-prevention technology becomes materially easier to deploy when a third party that bears loss—insurer, utility or portfolio owner—funds or subsidizes it. Portfolio buyers should value automatic shutoff, centralized monitoring and response more than standalone sensors.
falsifiers: UK insurers do not materially fund leak-prevention devices/services.
Water-sector institutions do not subsidize customer-side leak reduction.
Portfolio owners have no quantified reason to deploy prevention.
Existing vendors already own all insurer/property-manager workflows, leaving no independent commercial layer.
Claims-reduction evidence is too weak or vendor-only to justify prevention economics.

exact_analysis_questions.how_much_more_for_convenience_certainty_: The key payer is not the end user. Hiscox gives a £149 device plus annual engineer visit free; Admiral bulk-orders devices; Direct Line funds up to £500 after a qualifying loss; Aviva gives preferential commercial partner rates. This is direct evidence that insurers will spend to reduce future water loss.
exact_analysis_questions.which_problem_states_show_strongest_econ: Properties with prior escape-of-water loss; unoccupied units; multi-unit buildings where one leak damages multiple flats; portfolios with repeated EOW claims; commercial buildings with continuous hidden leakage.
exact_analysis_questions.current_options: LeakBot insurer bundles, insurer risk-management partner networks, Quensus/WINT/Leaksafe automatic shutoff, water-company leak support, property-manager maintenance teams, plumbers and insurer claims suppliers.
exact_analysis_questions.is_there_room_for_us: Little room in generic sensing/dashboard hardware. Possible narrow layer: prevention-funding eligibility across insurer + water-company schemes, post-loss retrofit orchestration, and evidence/renewal workflows for SME portfolios lacking enterprise risk teams.
exact_analysis_questions.best_gtm: B2B2C through brokers/insurers/property managers, not consumer Google Ads; post-claim trigger; insurer renewal/excess reduction workflow; utility leak-support eligibility; portfolio risk audit.
exact_analysis_questions.same_pattern_other_country: Norway B10 showed insurance discounts/deductible savings for water-stop systems. UK B11 independently shows free insurer-funded devices, bulk insurer deployment, direct post-loss retrofit funding and public water-sector subsidy.
exact_analysis_questions.why_country_difference: UK prevention is more institutionalized into insurer/vendor and regulator innovation channels than Norway's cabin-specific retail ecosystem. England's ~9.23m rented dwellings create large professional/organizational property pools.
exact_analysis_questions.what_does_it_reveal_about_country: UK property-risk prevention is becoming a B2B2C infrastructure market: insurer, broker, regulator, utility and portfolio owner may all touch the customer before a retail sensor seller does.
exact_analysis_questions.macro_pattern: When failure costs are externalized to a risk payer, distribution economics can invert: the technology is given free to the end user because avoided claims and retention justify payer-funded acquisition.
exact_analysis_questions.falsifier_result: Third-party subsidy mechanism strongly supported. Direct-to-landlord sensor thesis weakened because insurer-preferred vendors and portfolio systems are already mature. The open question is whether cross-payer funding/evidence orchestration is valuable enough to support an independent intermediary.

mechanism_candidates.statement: When the payer captures avoided loss, preventive technology can be distributed free to the end user at portfolio scale, replacing retail customer acquisition with B2B2C distribution.
mechanism_candidates.observed_context: Admiral committed 10,000 additional devices; Hiscox gives eligible customers a £149 device plus repair service free; LeakBot says insurers typically pay monthly per customer.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Find a non-water market where insurer/utility/lender funds preventive equipment across a customer book.

mechanism_candidates.statement: A sufficiently expensive prior loss can change insurer economics enough to unlock an explicit funded retrofit for future prevention.
mechanism_candidates.observed_statistic: up to £500 leak-detection funding after a covered water-damage loss exceeding £7,500.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Test flood resilience, burglary/security or fire prevention where insurers fund mitigation after claims.

mechanism_candidates.statement: The same physical risk can have multiple institutions willing to fund mitigation for different reasons: insurer claims, utility water loss, and property-owner operational disruption.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Look for another asset where utility + insurer + owner incentives overlap.

MC-RISK_PRICER_SUBSIDIZES_PREVENTION.new_evidence: UK insurers fund devices, repairs, preferential vendor access and post-loss retrofits; Ofwat funds customer-side leakage technology and Aviva is testing premium linkage.
MC-RISK_PRICER_SUBSIDIZES_PREVENTION.refined_statement: A third-party risk bearer can subsidize preventive technology when avoided claims/resource loss or retention value exceeds subsidy cost.

MC-ABSENCE_AMPLIFIES_DAMAGE_SEVERITY.new_evidence: Commercial insurer guidance says long-term unoccupancy can exacerbate undetected escape-of-water claims; multi-unit property cases show damage/relocation impacts when response is delayed.

MC-DETECTION_TO_INTERVENTION_VALUE_SHIFT.new_evidence: UK products increasingly bundle detection with plumber repair, automatic shutoff, portfolio dashboards and alarm/response workflows; sensor-only value is increasingly commoditized.

next_probe.selection_reason: B11 generated LOSS_EVENT_UNLOCKS_PREVENTION_BUDGET. UK flood insurance has a formal Build Back Better mechanism that can fund property-resilience measures after an insured flood. This is a high-information test of whether a claim itself creates a temporary, third-party-funded retrofit market with standards, contractors and measurable budget.
next_probe.hypothesis: After a covered catastrophic loss, insurer-funded resilience budgets create a high-intent retrofit cell in which specification/contractor coordination can be more valuable than pre-event consumer marketing.
falsifiers: Build Back Better uptake is negligible or insurer-controlled end-to-end.
Eligible measures are too standardized for intermediary value.
Insurer repair networks fully select contractors and products.
Post-claim customer choice is too constrained to support independent routing.
Available resilience funding is too small relative to retrofit complexity.
